Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows multiple, well-defined, bilateral pulmonary nodules in a patient with no history of cancer or systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss), which makes metastatic disease and active tuberculosis less likely. Pulmonary hyalinizing granuloma is a rare benign condition characterized by such slow-growing, well-circumscribed nodules that can present with cough and are often an incidental finding or associated with mild symptoms, fitting this clinical picture better than the other options which typically present with more systemic illness or different radiographic patterns (e.g., perilymphatic distribution for sarcoidosis).
